summary: Abandoned But Not Forgotten is a colourful 24-page picture book for children aged 7–12 about the landers, rovers and spacecraft that NASA left behind on the Moon, on Mars, on an asteroid and in deep space. Four friendly space guides take young readers to visit 13 explorers, from Apollo 11’s Eagle to the Ingenuity helicopter and Pioneer 10, which is still heading toward the stars. Each page has a short story, sound effects, real NASA photos and a “Mission File” that answers: where is it now? The book ends with a “Where Are They Now?” map, a quiz and a thank-you to the explorers. We turned NASA mission data from NSSDCA and NASA mission pages into stories that children can enjoy, because these explorers made historic discoveries but most kids have never heard of them. Our goal is to help kids learn about and remember these machines, because they are abandoned, but not forgotten.
details:
What it does: Our book tells the stories of 13 NASA missions whose equipment remains in space, in three chapters: The Moon (Apollo 11, 12 and 15, Surveyor 3), Mars (Viking 1, Pathfinder & Sojourner, Spirit & Opportunity, InSight, Ingenuity) and Beyond Mars (Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker, Pioneer 10, Kepler).
How it works: Each page has a short, easy-to-read story, sound effects like “Boing!” and “Thud!”, a real NASA photo and a Mission File with key facts and “Where is it now?”. Comparisons help kids understand the numbers; for example, Opportunity drove farther than a marathon. Four guide characters (Captain Whiskers, Professor Pup, Rocket Bunny and Ellie) talk to the reader on every page.
Benefits: It turns NASA mission data into a fun story for young children, and it reminds people that these explorers still exist and taught us a lot about our universe.
Why we chose this challenge: We wanted to remind everyone of the abandoned but not forgotten equipment in space, and we could also learn about them while doing this project.
Tools: Adobe Express (first version of the book and the AI character images). The final page layout, illustrations and demo slides were made with help from Claude, an AI assistant, as described in our SI section.
Future plans: Share it with schools and libraries, translate it into more languages, make an audiobook and a web version, and add explorers from other space agencies.
